newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen end flat after roller-coaster ride.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen end flat after roller-coaster ride.

text.p: The key three-month December Euroyen futures contract ended the day session on Wednesday unchanged after a roller-coaster ride of volatile trade.

"The market faces so many variables, including uncertainty over U.S. and Japanese interest rates and the divided outlook on the dollar/yen rate, that many are wary of being positioned either way for too long," said Shoji Kitta, president of Totan Research Co Ltd.

Speaking at a parliamentary committee meeting, Matsushita said on Wednesday that the central bank's policy in the late 1980s, when it took an easy monetary stance for a prolonged period, was one factor which brought about the so-called "bubble" economy of inflated asset prices.

The market is becoming increasingly wary of a possible rise in interest rates, but there is scepticism about whether the BOJ will actually be able to raise interest rates sooner than previously expected, traders said.
Totan Research's Kitta noted that the BOJ's assessment of the economy has become somewhat weaker recently.
"The market is still not sure whether the economy's recovery is full-blown," said a brokerage house trader.
Such renewed skepticism over the economy, combined with the steady cash Euroyen market, spurred dealers to buy back short positions built up during early trade.
The three-month cash Euroyen rate was last traded at 0.585 percent, little changed from Tuesday, money traders said.

The BOJ let the money market hold a fund surplus of 280 billion yen. The key unsecured overnight call rate was mostly traded at 0.50 percent, up from Tuesday's weighted average of 0.49 percent, as demand for short-term funds remained strong.
